3309:
** μεριμν-άω**,
**care for, be anxious about, meditate upon**, ἔργον μεριμνῶν ποῖον..; {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1124}}; especially of philosophers, τὰ <μὲν ἀ>φανῆ μ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 672; οἱ λεπτῶς μεριμνῶντες “Lyrica Adespota” 135, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.7.6; μ. περὶ τῆς τῶν πάντων φύσεως [prev. work] 1.1.14}}; πολλὰ μ. **to be cumbered with** many **cares**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.7.12; τοῖς μεριμνῶσίν τε καὶ λυπουμένοις 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Comicus 3; μηθὲν τὴν ἀλήθειαν μεριμνᾶν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.135 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, compare 2.143 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; μεριμνήσω ὑπὲρ τῆς ἁμαρτίας μου LXX.Psa.37(38).18; μ. εἰς τὴν αὔριον NT.Matt.6.34}}: c._infinitive_, **to be careful** to do, ὁ μεριμνήσας τὰ δίκαια λέγειν {{NT+5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.192: with _relative_ clause, πολλὰ μ. ὅπως μὴ λάθῃς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.23; μεριμνῶ πῶς κλαύσω “Anthologia Graeca” 9.148; μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε NT.Matt.6.25}}:—_passive_, **to be treated with anxious care,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|Anthologia Graeca 10.52 (6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus); τράπεζαι πολυτελῶς μεμεριμνημέναι 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.641c}}; ἔννοια, ἀμφισβήτησις μ., {{Refs 6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 22.26 “Intr.”, 44.1.3.}}
3312:
** μερ-ιστής**, οῦ, ὁ,
**divider, distributor,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Luke.12.14, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.176, “PMag.Leid.W.” 14.42}}; μ. χρόνων ζωῆς, of the lord of the horoscope, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 62.4}}:—_feminine_ **μερ-ίστρια**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|Scholia recentia 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 711.}}
3317:
** μεσο-νύκτιος**, ον,
**of** or **at midnight**, ἔκλειψις {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 367b26; ὥρα 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.31, compare “Anacreontea” 31.1: with a Verb, μεσονύκτιον δέξασθαί τινα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus}}**l.**7(6).5; μ. ὠλλύμαν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 914 (Lyric poetry)}}: _neuter_ as _adverb_, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.69}}: as _substantive_ **μεσο-νύκτιον**, τό, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.48, LXX.Judg.16.3, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 43, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 26, Vett. Val. 339.6; κατὰ τὸ μ. 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.5.42, NT.Act.16.25; μεσονυκτίου}}**at midnight,** {{NT|NT.Mark.13.35}}; μεσονύκτου seems to be _falsa lectio_ in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Sotion Paradoxographus p.185 W.—poetical word _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 36}}:—the spelling **μεσᾰνύκτιον** is variant in {{NT+3rd c.AD+|NT.Mark.13.35, compare “POxy.” 1768.6 (3rd c.AD).}}

3325:
** μεστ-όω**,
**fill full of**, with _genitive_ _of things_, ὀργῆς μ. τινά {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 280}}:—_passive_, **to be filled** or **full of**, κτύπου {{Refs|[prev. author] “El.” 713, compare “Ant.” 420}}; of persons, παρρησίας μεστοῦσθαι καὶ ἐλευθερίας {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 649b; ὕβρεώς τε καὶ ἀδικίας [prev. work] 713c: _absolutely_, 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 13}}; and in _medical_ sense, ἀγγεῖα μεμεστωμένα {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.394, compare 8.932.}}
3339:
** μεταμορφ-όω**,
**transform**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.479; ἑαυτὸν εἴς τι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 1.1}}; **disguise**, ἑαυτόν {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 4.41}}:—mostly in _passive_, **to be transformed,** {{NT+1st c.BC+|NT.Rom.12.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.52d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 11; εἰς θηρίων ἰδέαν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.81; εἰς Ἀπόλλωνα 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.559; εἰς ἰχθύν 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.334c; ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν NT.2Cor.3.18}}; **to be transfigured,** {{NT|NT.Matt.17.2, etc.}}
3347:
** μετέπειτα**,
_adverb_ **afterwards, thereafter**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.310, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.519, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.25, 3.36, 7.7, 197}}: rare in early Prose, ὁ μ. χρόνος {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 353c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1175a9; later, “OGI” 177.14 (Egypt, 1st c.BC), LXX.Jdt.9.5, LXX.3Mac.3.24, NT.Heb.12.17.}}
3350:
** μετοικ-εσία**, ἡ,
={μετοικία} 1, especially of the **captivity** of the Jews, {{LXX+NT|LXX.2Ki.24.16; ἡ μ. Βαβυλῶνος NT.Matt.1.11}}; also πλεόνων μ. 'the land o' the leal', {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“Anthologia Graeca” 7.731 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus).}}
3356:
** μετριο-πᾰθέω**,
**feel moderately, bear reasonably with**, τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσι καὶ πλανωμένοις {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.Heb.5.2: _absolutely_, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.113, 2.37, 45, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 12.3.2, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 3.235.}}
3365:
** μηδᾰμ-ῶς**,
_adverb_ of μηδαμός, ={μηδαμῇ}, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.83, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 339, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 278; μ. ἄλλως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 838d}}: in replies, as a strong _negative_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Prt.” 334d, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 217.}}
3369:
** μηδέ-πω**,
_adverb_ **nor as yet, not as yet**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author = 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus] “Pr.” 741, “Pers.” 435, etc.}}
3370:
** Μῆδος**, ὁ,
**Mede, Median**: hence, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Persian”, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.77, etc.}}
3371:
** μηκέτι**,
_adverb_, (formed from μή, ἔτι, with κ inserted on a false analogy with οὐκέτι) **no more, no longer, no further**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.292, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 174, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.5, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 805 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 12.75.29, etc.}}
3389:
** μητρ-ᾰλοίας**, ου, ὁ,
(ἀλοιάω) **striking one's mother**: hence, **matricide**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 153 (Lyric poetry), 210, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114a, etc.}}:—also written **μητρολῴας** or **μητρ-λώας**, {{NT|NT.1Tim.1.9, “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”}}
3399: **Miletus **, a Greek city in Caria, {{8th/7th c.BC|Iliad by Homer}} (from Middle LSJ)
